caption: The drawing depicts a geometric pattern likely meant as a textile or mosaic design. It features a grid of squares, each bordered in red. The main pattern, which occupies most of the image, consists of larger squares divided into smaller segments, separated by red-brown strips that resemble sashing. In each large square, there are three distinct types of smaller square motifs: a starburst pattern with alternating sharp triangular rays in red, yellow, and blue radiating from a small central star, a cluster of four rounded red petal shapes forming a symmetrical cross, and a motif with four comma-like golden shapes arranged in a pinwheel. Elongated yellow oval leaf shapes fill the spaces around the petals and starbursts. The grid is bordered by a thick, textured red band, and a narrower, wavy blue-and-white ornamental strip runs along the inside edge. In the top left, there is a smaller inset grid, bordered in red, composed of similar but more simplified motifs: blue circles with decorative elements, smaller starbursts, and yellow and red shapes. The background is an off-white or cream color, and the entire composition is arranged with symmetry and repetition.
title: Applique Quilt
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
